_note: The writing for The Wyrd Reading Together (two to nine people), in The Völva's register. Placeholders in curly braces are filled in by the site; keep them. Change any line and every reading changes with it. The free Compare page keeps the names of things (static/dynamics.js); the meaning is here and in lib/bond.json.
OPENING: This reading is for the people at one table: who sent each of you, what each of you wakes in the others, and the seasons you share. Read the story first. Everything after it is the decoder.
CLOSING: A bond is an engine too — two moving parts, a light wield, a dark wield, and a place where it breaks. Work the questions together, out loud if you can.
PROLOGUE_SUB: a silly story of how you ended up together
PROLOGUE_OPEN: Long before you met, each of you stood in the queue at the Well of Urðr — on different days, with no idea the others existed. Urðr keeps the ledger. She looked each of you up.
PROLOGUE_PERSON: {name} had been sent by {sent}, and chose {wore}.
PROLOGUE_TABLE_TWO: Neither of you knew that Skuld, who keeps what shall be, had already seated you at the same table. She does this on purpose. She calls it efficiency.
PROLOGUE_TABLE_MANY: None of you knew that Skuld, who keeps what shall be, had already seated all {n} of you at one table. She does this on purpose. She calls it efficiency; the arguments, she says, are good for everyone.
PROLOGUE_NOW: She checked the appointment books, as she does. Right now, {guests}. {season}
PROLOGUE_CLOSE: That is the story; the rest decodes it. Who Sits at the Table decodes who sent you. The Bond, why Skuld bothered. What You Wake in Each Other, why it felt like that from the start. The Old Match, How Your Bodies Meet and Your Numbers Together, the gifts. The Seasons You Share, the appointment book.

TABLE_SUB: each of you: who sent you, the costume, and the guest staying now
TABLE_INTRO: Each person's soul-planet is the one furthest through its sign — whoever sent them, and whoever holds the errand. The seat is the rising sign: the costume. The guest is the planet whose period runs that life now.
BOND_SUB: what it is for, its higher and lower paths, and every contact in words
BOND_INTRO: The bond, read twice: by the lunar mansions (Sukuyō), and by the planets between you. What it is for, how it lifts, how it drags — and how to weave the two.
WAKE_TITLE: What You Wake in Each Other
WAKE_SUB: where each of you lands in the other's life
WAKE_INTRO: Lay one chart over another and every planet of one person falls in a house of the other's. Two matter most. The soul-planet is what you were sent to do; the guest is what you are busy with now. Where they land in another's chart is the room of that life you walk into — whether either of you meant to.
WAKE_SOUL: {a}'s soul-planet, {planet}, lands in {b}'s {house} house: {life}. {a} brings {lends} there — and keeps bringing it.
WAKE_GUEST: For now, {a}'s guest, {lord}, stands in {b}'s {house} house: while it stays, {a} stirs {b}'s {life}.
UNKNOWN_HOUSES: {name}'s birth time is unknown, so {name}'s houses are counted from the Sun's sign.
SEASON_SUB: the next thirty years, chapter by chapter
SEASON_INTRO: Every life is a house with one planet in residence at a time, staying for years; each long stay divides into nine shorter ones. When two people share their days, their guests share them too — and how those planets get on is the weather between you. The tradition keeps a table of friends, neutrals and enemies; Rahu is read as Saturn, Ketu as Mars. Above the houses, the slow planets keep their own appointments: Saturn's and Jupiter's returns, the nodes', and Saturn's long crossing of the Moon. What follows walks the next thirty years chapter by chapter, then lays them flat, year by year.

same.label: the same planet
same.text: One planet runs both lives at once. You want the same things at the same time — a gift, until you want the same last thing.

allies.label: allies
allies.text: Your two guests are old friends: they lend each other tools, and the season between you runs easy. Build in it. Easy seasons are for building, not for resting.

friendly.label: warm on one side
friendly.text: One guest likes the other more than it is liked back. Warm on one side, cool on the other — the warm one should say so; the cool one should notice.

polite.label: polite strangers
polite.text: Polite strangers: nothing between you is blocked, and nothing is pushed. Whatever this season becomes, the two of you make it. No one else will.

uneasy.label: uneasy
uneasy.text: Your two guests don't quite trust each other, and small things rub. Say the small thing early, before it grows teeth.

odds.label: at odds
odds.text: Your two guests are at odds. The season tests the bond — and the test is the point: what survives it is load-bearing.

ASKS_SUB: for the table, in the order the reading asked them
ASKS: What was each of you sent to do — and does the other know?
Where does the other land in your life, and have you ever said so out loud?
What is this season asking the two of you to build — and what is it asking you to stop expecting?
When the next guest arrives, what will you wish you had already said?
PROLOGUE_GIFTS: Verðandi packed each of you a gift, the shadow folded into the same bag: {gifts}. Neither of you has found your own shadow yet. You will find each other's first — that is what tables are for.
PROLOGUE_BOOK: Skuld's book was already full. {turn} {mark} One year she underlined twice — {year} — and would not say why.
PROLOGUE_TURN: The next guest due is {lord}, for {name}, in {year}.
PROLOGUE_ERRAND: On the last page, under both your names, she wrote what the table is for: {errand}
PROLOGUE_ERRAND_PLAIN: to grow each other on purpose — and to say so out loud.

CHAPTER_LANDS: {a}'s {lord} stands in {b}'s {house} house: through these years, {a} stirs {b}'s {life}.

LORD_BOND.Sun: The Sun's years: {name} wants to be seen — by the world, and by the person across the table. Admiration said aloud feeds the bond; competition for the light starves it.
LORD_BOND.Moon: The Moon's years turn {name} toward home, feeling, family. More moods; more need. A bond's comfort is built in these years — or discovered missing.
LORD_BOND.Mars: Mars's years give {name} drive, heat, and the need for a project. Give the fire a job, or it will find one inside the bond.
LORD_BOND.Mercury: Mercury's years: {name} talks, trades, studies, plans. The bond lives in conversation now; keep the talk honest and the lists shared.
LORD_BOND.Jupiter: Jupiter's years bring {name} growth, teachers, faith, luck — sometimes children. The bond expands. Watch that it does not promise more than it can keep.
LORD_BOND.Venus: Venus's years bring {name} pleasure, beauty, love and money. The bond can bloom here — or be tested by someone, or something, lovely.
LORD_BOND.Saturn: Saturn's years ask {name} for work, weight and patience. Duty tests the bond; whatever survives is built in stone.
LORD_BOND.Rahu: Rahu's years make {name} hungry — for more, for new, for whatever was forbidden. Name the hunger before it names itself.
LORD_BOND.Ketu: Ketu's years pull {name} inward: letting go, the spiritual, the already-known. {name} may seem far away. The bond needs room here, not pursuit.

MARKS.saturn_return: {name}'s Saturn return, {when}. Saturn comes back to where it stood at {name}'s birth, and the life is audited: what was built on sand comes down. For the bond — recommit on purpose, or stop pretending.
MARKS.saturn_opposition: {name}'s Saturn opposition, {when}. Saturn halfway round: the midlife reckoning. The question put to the bond is whether it still fits the person {name} is becoming.
MARKS.jupiter_return: {name}'s Jupiter return, {when}. Jupiter comes home: growth, fresh faith, a door held open. A good year to begin something together.
MARKS.nodal_return: {name}'s nodal return, {when}. The nodes come round to their birth places and the hunger resets. What {name} reaches for changes direction; ask where, before it goes.
MARKS.sade_sati: {name}'s Sade Sati, {when}. Saturn crosses the three signs around {name}'s Moon: seven and a half years of pressure on the heart and the home. Carry each other's load. This is the long test, and it is passed slowly.

MARK_SHORT.sade_sati: Saturn begins its long crossing of {name}'s Moon

YEARS_INTRO: The same thirty years, laid flat: each person's long guest and shorter guest at mid-year, how the long guests get on, and the sky's appointments. Marked years are the ones to watch — both of you change at once, or the appointments pile up.
WATCH_NONE: No year piles up. The changes come one at a time.
NUM_SUB: life paths and names, side by side
NUM_INTRO: Each of you carries numbers — from the birth date and, where it was given, the full name at birth. Here they sit side by side. Every number stands on two planets, its Stavefall seat and its Vedic one; how those planets get on is how the numbers get on. How the numbers work →
NUM_PAIR_SAME: You share the number: one road, walked side by side. Recognition is easy — and so are the shared blind spots.
NUM_PAIR: By Stavefall the planets beneath them, {sa} and {sb}, are {ls}; by the Vedic seating, {va} and {vb}, they are {lv}.

NUM_MEANING.same: the numbers stand on one ground
NUM_MEANING.allies: the numbers pull the same way
NUM_MEANING.friendly: one number warms to the other more than it is warmed back
NUM_MEANING.polite: the numbers leave each other room
NUM_MEANING.uneasy: the numbers rub — say what each one needs
NUM_MEANING.odds: the numbers pull opposite ways, and the friction is the work

NUM_NO_NAME: Name numbers appear for everyone whose full name at birth was given.
KUTA_SUB: Ashtakoota, the eight-fold Jyotish match, in words
KUTA_INTRO: Jyotish matches two people by their Moons — the sign and the birth star each was born under. Eight measures; thirty-six points. Tradition reads the match in a fixed order, one partner first, and three of the measures change with that order, so this reading counts it both ways. A score is a starting point, not a verdict.

KUTA_VERDICT.strong: a strong match by the old count
KUTA_VERDICT.workable: a workable match by the old count
KUTA_VERDICT.demanding: a demanding match by the old count: the bond asks for conscious work

Varna.full: Your temperaments sit level: neither has to strain to respect the other.
Varna.none: Your footings differ. Respect here is chosen, not assumed — which makes it worth more.

Vashya.full: The pull runs both ways: each of you draws the other.
Vashya.part: One of you draws the other harder. The pull is real — and uneven.
Vashya.none: Neither of you naturally sways the other. Attraction here is built, not given.

Tara.full: Each birth star is kind to the other: the stars wish you well.
Tara.part: One star is kind, one is testing: luck favours the bond from one side.
Tara.none: Both stars count as testing. The bond makes its own luck.

Yoni.about: instinct and intimacy, read through the animal of each birth star
Yoni.full: Your instincts match: the animals of your birth stars are at ease together, and closeness comes without translation.
Yoni.part: Different animals that can learn each other. Intimacy takes patience — and is better for it.
Yoni.none: Your birth-star animals are old enemies. Instinct needs translating; tenderness has to be deliberate.

Graha Maitri.about: the friendship of the two Moon-sign lords: how your minds get on
Graha Maitri.full: Your Moon-sign lords are friends: your minds get on.
Graha Maitri.part: Your minds are civil rather than close; you understand each other by effort.
Graha Maitri.none: Your Moon-sign lords are at odds. You think differently — and arguments need rules.

Gana.full: Your natures can share a house.
Gana.part: One nature is gentler than the other; the fiercer one learns restraint, or the gentler one learns to leave the room.
Gana.none: Your natures clash. The bond needs agreed limits, written down if necessary.

Bhakoot.about: the distance between your Moon signs: love, money and the life you build
Bhakoot.full: Your Moon signs sit at an easy distance for love, money and the life you build.
Bhakoot.none: Your Moon signs sit at a testing distance (2–12, 5–9 or 6–8). Be explicit about money and family — vagueness is where it costs.

Nadi.full: Your pulses differ, and balance each other.
Nadi.none: You share a Nadi — one bodily pulse — the tradition's most serious single mismatch. Living closely, you can wear out each other's constitution. Give each other rest, and room.

HD_SUB: your two designs, side by side, in words
HD_INTRO: Lay one bodygraph over another. Some channels light only when you are together; some you share; some one of you carries for both. Where one of you is defined and the other open, the open one feels the defined one's current amplified — and can mistake it for their own.
HD_TYPES: {a} is a {ta} with {aa} authority; {b} is a {tb} with {ab} authority. Together your two bodies make one field: a {tc}.

HD_KIND.em: Electromagnetic: each of you holds one end of the channel, and together it lights. This is the spark between you — and the place you most easily rub.
HD_KIND.comp: Companionship: you both carry the channel whole. Here nothing needs explaining; you share one way of being.
HD_KIND.dom: Dominance: one of you carries the whole channel and the other neither gate. Here one leads, and the other learns the current from outside.
HD_KIND.promise: Compromise: one of you carries the whole channel, the other only one of its gates. The whole current tends to win; the other gives way — and should notice when giving way costs too much.

HD_COND: {a}'s defined {centre} ({does}) is amplified in {b}, whose {centre} is open. For {b}: {open}
HD_COND_NONE: You are defined and open in the same centres; little amplification passes between you.
HD_OPEN_BOTH: Open in both of you: {centres}. Here the two of you take in the world together — other people and places colour these centres for you both.
